issueComment.body:
Additional observed mutation-adapter boundary in TOML development run `p6vm5s00w6`, attempt `q3xbl70q20`, source `525d2e09f8168a3bdd7e513e26d4c80b363123e5`, harness `274ec49595d60f663249d61ab35a0806fe29aff0`.

This is separate from this issue's original browser `newuidmap` rejection. The source-owner nonroot mutation adapter reached a root-owned `/work` tmpfs. Every one of its `9037` shard attempts emitted:

```text
# Source container copy diagnostics
rsync: [generator] chgrp "/work/." failed: Operation not permitted (1)
rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (see previous errors) (code 23)
```

The native report has `3062` distinct mutant identities, all `runtimeError`; these are infrastructure-derived statuses before mutant assertions, not completed source mutation outcomes. All native identities reconcile with all shard manifests and `18338` mutant assignments. The full byte-identical native report is durably retained as `doc/audit/depot-toml-mutation-native-2026-10-17.evidence.json.gz`, uncompressed SHA256 `e3b1023242fb838e30ad22ce1aa0c593f412401be141901594af34c484177bce`.

The original source command ran for `2640500.405168` milliseconds and failed. It did not reach the one-hour wrapper deadline. Final scoped cleanup verified no owned process group or labeled containers remained. Provider interval for this attempt is `2738592` milliseconds at `16x64`. Matching before/after source proof, artifact `01a148a6-f383-7601-97bb-5e2f44ea27ff` and SHA256 `8480e110dfd7c09a672aa6786fa9469b482e08e0df8c8c336e1b55264ce5059d`, every log hash, instrumentation limits, and cleanup are retained in `doc/audit/depot-toml-reconciliation-2026-10-17.evidence.json` (commit `893b26838e`).

The complete corrected containers adapter from `d098532a5b6946231daf3c4f43e38444359a307e` is being exercised by a bounded actual TOML pilot. That adapter's separate logger consumer already passed in `360d91ht6w`. This observation does not close browser coverage, claim a passing TOML campaign, or merge the distinct `#1116` user-namespace unmount and `#1117` baked-metadata incidents.

## Observed failure

Run `p9r4xl6n12`, attempt `ltfw0kr3cd`, ran the frozen TOML source
`525d2e09f8168a3bdd7e513e26d4c80b363123e5` through harness `409e6ec10600958a5eba45200944ce25eefe7749`.
The file-enforcer container check completed with failure after `79620.70287899999` milliseconds (#1070).
TOML mutation started at `2026-10-17T04:36:53.885Z`.
The provider canceled the job at `2026-10-17T05:04:22.162Z` because it exceeded 30 minutes.
TOML mutation has no terminal result or retained active log artifact.
Independent file-enforcer mutation never ran.
That unexecuted task has a separate historical source path failure in #1068.

## Diagnosed harness boundary

The generic executor buffers stdout/stderr to a file and awaits each child exit without a per-check deadline.
The container wave defaults to a single worker and sequences independent checks in one job.
The mutation runner permits each container session to last 1800 seconds,
and its campaign can start further sessions and retries.
The outer 30-minute job includes preparation and the preceding container check.
The job timeout skipped artifact upload and the final source immutability proof.
The mutation campaign's internal cause is not established.
Neither an out-of-memory kill nor a mutation-source defect has been proved by this timeout.

## Required behavior

Each selected container or mutation gate must run independently,
retain its exact source command and actual outcome,
and preserve incremental logs, source identity, provider usage, and scoped container diagnostics.
A deadline for one gate must leave independent gates eligible to run.
A source failure remains failed.
A started gate's bounded timeout remains timed out, never passed.
A prerequisite timeout before the selected gate starts must retain that distinction.

## Evidence and replay

`doc/audit/depot-toml-reconciliation-2026-10-17.evidence.json` retains the frozen manifest,
all emitted events, exact diagnostics, artifact digests, and provider intervals.
The captured-trace assertion `mise run reconcile-toml -- --assert-complete` fails on missing terminal evidence.
The canceled attempt consumed `1816904` provider milliseconds at `16x64`;
this failed usage remains in the audit.

## Duplicate search

An all-state GitHub search for TOML mutation timeout found #247 and #479,
which do not describe this executor deadline, evidence-retention, or independent-check scheduling boundary.
Historical #1068 and #1070 remain distinct source failures.

## Actual source producer failure

At immutable source `525d2e09f8168a3bdd7e513e26d4c80b363123e5`, the unchanged `chainMethodReplacements` function emits non-string replacement text for inherited Object prototype names. A direct source consumer on Node `v26.12.0` uses structurally valid call/member AST nodes and measures:

- `startsWith`: one string replacement, `endsWith` (positive control).
- `unmappedMethod`: no replacement (ordinary unmapped control).
- `toString`, `constructor`, and `hasOwnProperty`: one function-valued replacement each.

`METHOD_SWAPS` is a plain object. `METHOD_SWAPS[name]` reads inherited prototype properties, and the `!== undefined` check accepts those functions. This violates the declared string replacement contract in `package/cli/mutation-test/src/engine/types.ts`. The same lookup remains present in current main source. No application source edit is included.

## Observed serialized consequence

The full native report from TOML run `p6vm5s00w6` contains these three `method` candidates with original `toString` and no serialized `replacement` property:

- `583eb11824f58d9f`: `src/basic-escape.ts:76:14`.
- `21d87c25edc6d4b7`: `src/conformance/decode-leaf.ts:144:9`.
- `e6fbbc25cf51fa14`: `src/values.ts:133:17`.

Their description includes `swapped .toString with .function toString() { [native code] }`. JSON serialization omits a function-valued property. The complete native report is retained byte-for-byte in `doc/audit/depot-toml-mutation-native-2026-10-17.evidence.json.gz`, with raw SHA256 `e3b1023242fb838e30ad22ce1aa0c593f412401be141901594af34c484177bce`.

All cloud shard attempts failed copying into `/work` before mutant assertions. Their `runtimeError` statuses are infrastructure-derived; this report does not attribute those cloud failures to the invalid replacement. The direct source operator consumer proves the independent producer defect.

## Acceptance

- Only declared method-swap entries emit replacement strings.
- Inherited Object names remain outside the swap family.
- Native mutant serialization retains a valid string replacement for every emitted candidate.
- Positive mapped-method and unmapped-method controls continue to exercise the boundary.
- Preserve the historical three malformed candidates and the separate container infrastructure failure.

## Duplicate search

All-state current-repository searches covered `mutation toString`, `mutation prototype`, and `mutation replacement`. No matching operator-lookup incident was found. Issues `#1116` and `#1117` concern independent container prerequisites.

## Summary

The checked-in root `mise.toml` is generated from `mise.no-env.toml`, but its package-bin `PATH` entries are discovered from whichever `packages/*/*/node_modules/.bin` directories happen to exist on the machine running file-enforcer.

That makes a tracked generated file depend on install/build history rather than repository metadata. Two worktrees at the same commit can generate different `mise.toml` files.

## Reproduction

Verified on `main` at `4d1d66a0e2440f4402ea1eb454db6e49aacfbc48`.

In the clean detached checkout, no package-local bin directory exists:

```sh
find packages -mindepth 4 -maxdepth 4 -type d \
  -path '*/node_modules/.bin' | wc -l
# 0
```

The committed `mise.toml`, however, contains 32 package-local bin paths. After a frozen pnpm install in a disposable worktree, 21 package-local bin directories existed. Running the generator with the repository's pinned Node 26.4.0 succeeded but rewrote the tracked file:

```sh
node file-enforcer.config.ts
git diff --numstat -- mise.toml
# 2  13  mise.toml
```

The rewritten file contained exactly the 21 directories materialized in that worktree. It removed 13 committed paths and added 2 paths that were absent from the committed snapshot.

## Root cause

`file-enforcer.config.ts:549-575` constructs `_.path` with:

```ts
[
  'node_modules/.bin',
  ...(await Array.fromAsync(glob('packages/*/*/node_modules/.bin'))),
]
```

The glob observes generated filesystem state. Whether a package has a local `.bin` directory can vary with filtered installs, platform-specific dependencies, whether workspace bin targets existed when pnpm linked them, and prior build/reinstall history.

## Expected behavior

Generating repository-owned files at a fixed commit should not depend on ambient `node_modules` shape. A documented fresh install followed by `sync:files` should leave the worktree clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- Package-bin `PATH` entries are derived deterministically from workspace/package metadata, or the dynamic state is moved out of the checked-in file.
- Entries are emitted in a stable order.
- A fixture proves that identical manifests generate byte-identical `mise.toml` output when the set of materialized `.bin` directories differs.
- A fresh frozen install followed by `node file-enforcer.config.ts` leaves `mise.toml` unchanged.
- Filtered installs and platform-specific optional dependencies cannot add or remove tracked lines.

## Deduplication

no semantic match. Fresh searches for `generateMiseToml`, `node_modules/.bin mise.toml`, `sync:files mise`, and `_.path file-enforcer` returned only unrelated issues (#46, #99, #163, #246, #257, and file-enforcer issues about other behavior).
rows.title: fix(build): generate mise PATH entries from workspace metadata, not ambient node_modules

## Context

rows.body:
## Summary

The file-enforcer staleness-manifest lock has a publication race: one process creates the lock directory and writes `owner.json`, while a contender can observe the directory and parse `owner.json` before the write is complete.

This makes the package's own parallel unit task fail intermittently with a persistence error such as:

```text
StalenessManifestPersistenceError: Invalid .../staleness-manifest.json.lock/owner.json: Unexpected end of JSON input
```

## Reproduction

Verified on `main` at `4d1d66a0e2440f4402ea1eb454db6e49aacfbc48` with Node 26.4.0:

```sh
mise run //packages/dev-script/file-enforcer:test:unit
```

The failure reproduced in `src/io/write-toml.unit.test.ts` when test files ran in parallel. Running that test file alone passed, which isolates the failure to inter-file lock contention.

## Root cause

- `staleness-manifest-lock.ts:151-167` creates the lock directory, then records owner metadata as a separate operation.
- A contender that receives `EEXIST` immediately invokes stale-lock recovery.
- `staleness-manifest-lock-owner.ts:133-149` writes JSON directly to the final `owner.json` path.
- `staleness-manifest-lock-owner.ts:168-198` immediately reads and parses that file; an empty or partial snapshot is treated as permanently invalid instead of as an in-progress lock publication.

The directory's existence therefore becomes visible before its owner metadata is safely readable.

## Expected behavior

A live lock being initialized by another process must be treated as contended, not corrupt or stale.

## Acceptance criteria

- Owner metadata is published atomically, or missing/partial owner metadata during lock initialization is handled as a bounded retryable state.
- A malformed owner file that is not an in-progress publication remains diagnosable and does not silently bypass stale-lock safety.
- A deterministic regression test exercises the directory-created/metadata-not-yet-published interleaving.
- The package unit task is stable under repeated parallel runs.
rows.title: fix(file-enforcer): manifest lock contenders can read a partially written owner.json

## Summary

Five manifests that declare themselves public have six runtime dependency edges to workspace packages marked `private: true`.

Publishing any affected consumer with pnpm's normal `workspace:*` rewrite would leave external consumers depending on packages that the current repository configuration forbids publishing.

## Current graph

Verified on `main` at `4d1d66a0e2440f4402ea1eb454db6e49aacfbc48`:

| Public consumer | Private runtime dependency |
| --- | --- |
| `@monochromatic-dev/agent-harnesses-shared-session-discovery` | `@monochromatic-dev/module-logger` |
| `@monochromatic-dev/agent-harnesses-shared-shell-command-analyzer` | `@monochromatic-dev/module-logger` |
| `@monochromatic-dev/dev-script-watch-restart` | `@monochromatic-dev/module-logger` |
| `@monochromatic-dev/module-test` | `@monochromatic-dev/module-fs-path` |
| `@monochromatic-dev/module-test` | `@monochromatic-dev/module-logger` |
| `@monochromatic-dev/module-toml-edit` | `@monochromatic-dev/module-logger` |

The consumer manifests use `private: false`; several also have `publishConfig.access: public`. The two dependency manifests use `private: true`.

## Impact

- The public/private boundary is not closed under runtime dependencies.
- Release automation tracked by #159 cannot safely publish these packages as currently described.
- A package can pass all workspace tests because pnpm links the private dependency locally, then fail for a registry consumer whose install cannot obtain that dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- Record the intended external boundary for each of the five consumers.
- If a consumer remains public, every runtime workspace dependency is made externally resolvable by publishing it, bundling/internalizing it, or removing the edge.
- If a consumer is not intended to ship, mark it `private: true` and remove contradictory public publish metadata.
- Add a workspace graph check that rejects a non-private package's `dependencies` or `optionalDependencies` edge to a private workspace package.
- The check reports the complete dependency path and distinguishes runtime edges from harmless dev-only edges.

Related: #59, #159.

## Deduplication

no semantic match in the 257-issue corpus or fresh searches for `publishable packages private workspace packages`, `unpublished private packages`, `watch-restart private publish`, and `private dependencies publish`. Related policy trackers #59 and #159 do not inventory or enforce runtime dependency closure.

Audited at `4d1d66a0e2440f4402ea1eb454db6e49aacfbc48`.

## Problem

Both Cargo publish detectors can mistake an unavailable baseline for a version bump and start a live publication.

For `forbidden-strings`, `.github/workflows/cargo-publish.yml:40-46` checks out only two commits. Lines 59-63 leave `before=''` when `github.event.before` is absent from the shallow clone, and line 74 treats `before != after` as a version change. The nested-wayland-session detector duplicates the same behavior at lines 301-304 and 317-330.

A push containing two or more commits normally has a `before` SHA older than those two checked-out commits. Force pushes and other shallow-history edge cases have the same problem. Because the workflow is path-filtered to `Cargo.toml`, a multi-commit dependency or metadata edit with an unchanged version can set `should_publish=true`. On push events, the publish jobs are live rather than dry-run, so this can attempt an unintended crate upload or release instead of failing closed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Explicitly fetch and verify `github.event.before`, or use sufficient history, before comparing versions.
- [ ] On a normal push, an unavailable nonzero `before` SHA fails closed instead of becoming an empty version.
- [ ] Define initial-branch-push and force-push behavior explicitly; do not infer a bump solely from a missing baseline.
- [ ] Share one tested detector implementation between both crates.
- [ ] Test single- and multi-commit pushes with changed and unchanged versions, an initial push, and an unavailable baseline.

## Deduplication

Checked semantically against all 176 open and 81 closed issues, plus fresh open/closed searches for `fetch-depth version bump` and `cargo publish before SHA`. No existing issue owns this defect.
rows.title: fix(release): fetch and verify the before SHA before Cargo version-bump detection

## Original problem

The isolated Depot trial's `trial:depot:ci:source-identity` helper at
`4c4063e78bc9aaed8e293c1b478db089d6eef0ce` checked source HEAD,
tracked Git status,
selected metadata bytes,
and before/after identities.
Its configured-input enumeration omitted tracked inputs:

- `.cargo/config.toml`.
- `package/music-player/android-app/rust/Cargo.toml`.
- `package/music-player/android-app/rust/Cargo.lock`.

The actual original helper accepted each independently changed omitted input in a disposable clone
when `assume-unchanged` hid the edit from Git status.
Each after command exited zero with the saved identity.
A changed hashed `mise.lock` under the same flag was rejected,
so the byte-comparison control was capable of detecting the change when its path was included.

The old helper also relied on Git status for ordinary tracked paths outside its metadata hash subset.
Its source contained no rejection of `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` exclusions.
The ordinary-source masking risk is a source-audited boundary of that original implementation;
the original 15-control record directly reproduced the metadata omissions,
not an additional old-revision ordinary-source test.
The final 12-control record directly measures both flags on ordinary source outside the metadata set.

This is a trial-helper integrity incident.
No provider run was proved to have changed these files or enabled the flags.
The historical source bytes were not repaired or rewritten.

## Verified corrections

- `c0baaeb1d6` expands metadata enumeration to root configuration,
  root `.cargo/` inputs,
  and nested metadata inside selected or artifact-prerequisite packages.
- `faf388e838737e6b08b9a8075cdcbf4b34f02b2b` uses NUL-delimited tracked paths.
  The actual helper hashes the three former omissions and rejects their hidden edits.
  A private metadata path containing spaces,
  single/double quotes,
  and a newline is hashed correctly;
  its hidden edit is rejected and its restored after control passes.
- `a07d84a129f0dd16861551adfb76b1a3bbc4083d` independently rejects index exclusions before tracked status.
  The actual helper rejects both unchanged flags and hidden edits to ordinary
  `package/music-player/truepeak-core/src/lib.rs`,
  which is outside the metadata hash list.
  Git status is empty in each rejection control.
  Both `assume-unchanged` and `skip-worktree` are covered.
  Restored ordinary source and unflagged adversarial metadata pass.

The final diagnostic is:

```text
Immutable source index must not hide tracked inputs with assume-unchanged or skip-worktree flags
```

The metadata hashes remain a selected evidence subset,
not an exhaustive byte inventory of every tracked source file.
The independent index invariant prevents those flags from hiding paths outside the subset.
Its deliberate tradeoff is that indexed exclusions are incompatible with this fully checked immutable-source gate,
even when the excluded bytes currently equal HEAD.
Untracked files and ignored build outputs remain outside this helper's contract.

## Acceptance and retained evidence

- [x] The omitted root and nested Cargo metadata is hashed and compared to committed Git blobs.
- [x] NUL path boundaries preserve spaces,
  quotes,
  and newlines through enumeration,
  blob reads,
  JSON persistence,
  and identity comparison.
- [x] Both index flags are rejected for unchanged ordinary source and for hidden ordinary-source edits.
- [x] Both historical before/after pairs remain accepted:
  `cb95cf6d785c3073c192b95f0632cdae7b910894` and `3434eaa455d569c18b52cf15100f77f9db251d21`.
  Their source heads,
  trees,
  configured bytes,
  manifest hashes,
  and clean tracked status are retained.
- [x] The original 15-control,
  metadata/path repair 19-control,
  and index-invariant 12-control records remain separate.
- [x] The indexed-exclusion tradeoff and selected metadata hash boundary are explicit.

The pushed default-branch evidence is:

- [Original 15 controls](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/blob/main/doc/audit/depot-source-identity-controls-2026-10-17.evidence.json),
  committed in `1022ae62aae4b37871e393754e6fd7984be6e219`.
- [Metadata/path repair 19 controls](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/blob/main/doc/audit/depot-source-identity-repaired-controls-2026-10-17.evidence.json),
  committed in `858d9fb21ed0902d9b3e5e3208e13e82b0be4a5e`.
- [Index-invariant 12 controls](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/blob/main/doc/audit/depot-source-identity-index-controls-2026-10-17.evidence.json),
  committed in `c1eee586d54d30a081897ee704473ac71b6115ed`.
- [Troubleshooting diagnosis and scope](https://github.com/Aquaticats/Monochromatic/blob/main/doc/troubleshooting/depot-historical-checkout-bootstrap.md#source-identity-input-coverage).

Verification used actual task invocations and disposable mutation fixtures.
Shared historical source worktrees and shared harness task bytes remained unchanged during the controls.
No cloud run or broad application test suite was dispatched for this verification.
Closing this helper-specific incident does not claim production workflow adoption,
passing application tests,
or a final coherent provider replay.

## Duplicate search

All-state current-repository searches covered `"source identity"`,
`"source-identity"`,
`"immutable" "checkout"`,
`"immutable source"`,
`"assume-unchanged"`,
`"skip-worktree"`,
and `"index" "mask"`.
No matching helper incident was found.
The source-identity mentions in #1108 concern a missing desktop tool wave;
#1113 concerns mutation timeout and lost evidence.
Neither is this input enumeration/index-exclusion incident.

rows.body:
## Goal

Evaluate Cloudflare Workers Cache for public Git LFS object delivery in
`package/config/lfs-r2-worker`,
then adopt it only if correctness, account availability, and measured benefit justify it.

This is backlog work for when maintainer capacity is available.
No deployment, account change, or performance experiment has been performed for this issue.
The findings are documentation and source inspection as of 2026-10-10.
Documentation updated on 2026-10-03 is not evidence of the feature's launch date.

## Why this is worth evaluating

Workers Cache can serve eligible responses before Worker execution.
For a cache hit, the documented design avoids running the handler and its R2 reads.
It includes tiered caching and concurrent-request collapsing.
This could reduce repeated object reads and response latency for public README images and LFS downloads.
There is no measured benefit for this deployment yet.

Cache hits still count at the standard Workers request rate.
They do not incur Worker CPU execution.
Enabling Workers Cache also makes normally free static-asset and Worker-to-Worker requests
billable at the standard request rate if those paths are used.
See [Workers Cache pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/#pricing).
Account eligibility, including whether this deployment's Free plan can use the feature,
must be verified before treating it as a free optimization.

Primary documentation:
- [Workers Cache overview](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/)
- [Configuration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/configuration/)
- [Limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/limitations/)

## Existing caching behavior

“Workers is cached by default” depends on which path serves the bytes:

- [Workers Static Assets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/)
  automatically caches uploaded static assets.
  This package instead streams objects through an R2 binding.
- An outgoing Worker `fetch()` can use the CDN cache according to eligibility and zone rules.
  This does not by itself bypass the incoming Worker handler.
  See [how the cache works](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/how-the-cache-works/).
- R2 binding calls such as `env.BUCKET.get()` and `env.BUCKET.head()`
  access R2 directly.
  They do not automatically use its public-domain CDN cache.
  See [R2 consistency and caching](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/reference/consistency/#caching).
- Successful object responses already include
  `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
  That permits client caching but does not itself install shared edge caching ahead of this handler.
- The separate Workers Cache feature requires explicit `cache.enabled = true`.
  “Every entrypoint by default” describes inheritance after enablement.
  Omitting or removing the cache configuration disables it.
  The documentation specifies Wrangler 4.69.0 or later;
  verify the actual tool version used to deploy.

## Current package source

Recheck these files before implementation because the repository may have moved:

- `package/config/lfs-r2-worker/wrangler.toml`:
  `workers_dev = true`, one `BUCKET` R2 binding, no cache configuration.
- `package/config/lfs-r2-worker/src/index.ts`:
  anonymous GET/HEAD on `/<oid>` and `/<oid>/<path>`;
  suffix selects media type.
  POST handles the LFS batch API.
  PUT on the bare oid reaches the authenticated upload handler.
- `package/config/lfs-r2-worker/src/object-route.ts`:
  normal GET calls `BUCKET.get(oid)`;
  HEAD and matching conditional requests call `BUCKET.head(oid)`.
  Successful replies carry the immutable policy and quoted-oid ETag.
  Missing-object 404 replies currently have no explicit cache policy.
  Upload authorization is checked before `BUCKET.put()`.

This describes checked-in code, not independently inspected live account configuration.
Related context: #476, #491, and #492 concern LFS-backed Markdown images and post-push URL validation.

## Correctness and operational questions

### Cache eligibility and upload boundaries

Only GET/HEAD are eligible for Workers Cache.
POST batch requests and PUT uploads must continue to execute normally.
Keep upload authentication intact and verify rejected writes with disposable fixtures.
Do not infer that successful public caching proves write authorization is correct.

Cache hits bypass application code.
If public downloads later acquire access control, per-request validation or audit requirements,
revisit the design before relying on handler checks or handler logs for every request.

### Negative caching and upload visibility

The documented default TTL for a cacheable 404 without explicit freshness headers is 180 seconds.
A request for a missing oid followed by its upload could therefore keep returning cached absence.

Give missing-object responses an explicit policy such as `Cache-Control: no-store`,
unless a deliberately chosen alternative is justified.
Cover normal GET, HEAD, and conditional missing-object branches,
plus invalid-route responses where appropriate.
Verify “missing, then upload, then immediately fetch” through the real cache.

### HEAD changes the origin work

On a cold HEAD request, Workers Cache converts the request reaching the Worker to GET,
fills the cache with the response body, and strips the body for the HEAD caller.
GET and HEAD share the cache entry.

The current uncached HEAD only reads R2 metadata.
Enabling caching can turn the first metadata probe into a full object read.
Measure this separately, especially for large objects and post-push URL checks.

### Ranges and object size

The current documented Workers Cache response-size cap is 512 MB for all accounts.
Do not import the larger Enterprise limit from the general CDN documentation.
Objects beyond the limit need a functioning uncached path.

Worker-produced 206 responses are not stored.
The documented cache path strips Range before Worker invocation,
stores a complete 200 representation, and can serve byte ranges from it as 206 or 416.
The current GET handler streams the whole object and does not implement a Range branch.
Test Range and If-Range semantics explicitly before promising resumable-download improvements.

### Cache identity and response metadata

The default key includes the path, query, and Worker version;
hostname is excluded.
Review the precise documented key before changing defaults.

Do not collapse all paths to oid alone without preserving representation metadata:
`/<oid>` and suffixed URLs can intentionally have different Content-Type values.
Test bare, image-suffixed, and differently suffixed URLs for the same object.
Avoid enabling cross-version reuse until changes to headers and response behavior are accounted for.

Do not assume arbitrary request headers, cookies, or future personalization are safely isolated by the default key.
Keep this evaluation scoped to genuinely public, identical representations.
Requests carrying Authorization can still be cacheable with response directives such as
public, must-revalidate, or s-maxage; the presence of that request header is not a blanket safeguard.

### Deletion, replacement, and rollback

A cached object may remain available after its R2 object is deleted.
The existing conditional path checks that an object still exists before returning 304;
a cache hit may no longer reach that check.

Define deletion and purge behavior explicitly.
If immediate removal is required, test the purge path and its propagation.
Content-addressed naming is the intended contract;
do not assume that naming alone prevents an upload from replacing an existing oid.

Document how to disable caching, purge retained entries when necessary,
and verify uncached behavior after rollback.
Keep the versioned cache-key default initially.

## Proposed evaluation

1. Confirm current feature status, exact account/plan eligibility, limits, pricing,
   and Wrangler support using current official documentation and the actual deployment account.
2. Build a disposable deployment and bucket using public test fixtures.
   Keep production objects and upload credentials out of the experiment.
3. Establish a cache-disabled baseline and run the same tests with cache enabled.
   Use the package's existing build and test tasks.
4. Observe MISS/HIT behavior and independently count handler execution and R2 reads.
   Handler logs alone cannot count requests served before the handler.
5. Measure cold and warm latency distributions, Worker CPU, request accounting,
   R2 GET/HEAD operations, bytes fetched on cold HEAD, and concurrent-miss behavior.
   Record client location, concurrency, fixture size, versions, sample counts, and run-to-run spread.
6. Compare results against leaving the current implementation unchanged.
   The alternative Cache API runs inside the Worker and requires explicit lookup/storage;
   do not conflate its behavior or tiering with Workers Cache.
7. Adopt, defer, or reject based on measured tradeoffs, recording the result and operational runbook.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Account availability and costs are verified without assuming Free-plan eligibility.
- [ ] Cache-disabled and enabled configurations are recorded and reproducible.
- [ ] Repeated GET shows actual cache reuse with matching bytes, ETag, Content-Type, and Content-Length.
- [ ] HEAD returns no body; cold HEAD's full-fetch cost is measured and accepted.
- [ ] Conditional requests, missing objects, and missing-then-upload behavior remain correct.
- [ ] Bare and suffixed URLs cannot contaminate each other's media types.
- [ ] Range, If-Range, large-object bypass, and any documented cache limits are checked.
- [ ] Authenticated and rejected PUTs and batch operations retain their behavior.
- [ ] Deletion, purge, version changes, and rollback have tested semantics.
- [ ] Latency and operations are compared with the unchanged baseline; no savings are claimed from cache headers alone.
- [ ] Package tests and scoped type checks pass for any eventual implementation.
- [ ] The issue records an adopt/defer/reject decision and the remaining limitations.

## Scope

This issue evaluates and, if justified, integrates public LFS-response caching.
It does not require moving authoritative DNS, migrating the main website,
changing mirror providers, making private objects public, or upgrading a subscription.

rows.body:
# Summary

A literal recursive copy of this repository does not produce an independent,
relocatable checkout.
Most source work succeeds from a copied path on the same prepared Fedora host,
but copied Git administration, generated artifacts, tracked configuration,
and user-global integrations retain dependencies on the source checkout.
A copy can therefore appear healthy while silently reading from or mutating the original repository.

The supported goal should be a **relocatable checkout**, not a literally self-contained machine image.
The destination must be independent of the source checkout while retaining explicit seams for host tools,
user trust, secrets, models, external datasets, and integration ownership.

# Measured reproduction

The source tree was audited and copied to a disposable directory on the same Btrfs filesystem with:

```sh
# From repository root
cp --archive --reflink=always \
  /var/home/user/Monochromatic \
  /var/home/user/temp/agent/Monochromatic-cp-audit-20260722
```

Measured source state:

- Logical tree size: 131 GB.
- Tracked files: 6,433.
- Ignored entries reported by Git status: 400,051.
- Git LFS tracked files: 36.
- Symbolic links: 3,737.
- Linked-worktree administrative records under `.git/worktrees`: 20.
- Submodules: none.
- Git object alternates: none.

The Btrfs copy completed in 58 seconds.
All 6,433 tracked-file SHA-256 records matched between source and destination.
The destination also passed these probes:

- Real Git and the repository's `cli-git` wrapper both ran `status` successfully.
- `git lfs fsck` reported `Git LFS fsck OK`.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc --version` ran and module resolution selected TypeScript from the destination tree.
- After explicitly trusting the copied Mise configuration in isolated trust state,
  `mise run //package/module/async-time:buildAndTest` built the package and passed both unit tests.

This proves that ordinary package work can succeed after relocation.
It does not prove that the copied checkout is independent.

# Findings

## Copied Git administration remains coupled to the source

The destination's `git worktree list --porcelain` retained 20 linked-worktree registrations whose roots remained
under `/var/home/user/Monochromatic*`, `/var/home/user/worktrees`, `/var/home/user/mono-wt`, and another temporary path.
Every copied `.git/worktrees/*/gitdir` file retained an absolute source-host path.

The main tree also contains a nested linked worktree:

```text
.claude/worktrees/translation-repair/.git
```

Its copied contents remained:

```text
gitdir: /var/home/user/Monochromatic/.git/worktrees/translation-repair
```

A Git command inside that nested directory therefore still targets the original repository.
The copied root repository is usable for ordinary operations,
but worktree enumeration, branch ownership, worktree mutation, and `cli-git` observation are not independent.

The copied `.git/config` also contains a credential-bearing Git LFS URL.
The credential value must never appear in logs, reports, tests, or this issue.
Copying `.git` propagates that secret to every destination.
The credential must be revoked or rotated immediately,
then supplied through a credential helper or explicit secret injection rather than a URL in local repository config.

`/usr/bin/git fsck --full --no-dangling` failed identically in the source and destination with
`Could not read ...` and
`failed to parse commit ... from object database for commit-graph` diagnostics.
This is pre-existing source Git metadata state rather than copy corruption,
but a byte copy preserves it.
A newly constructed independent repository can avoid carrying stale commit-graph data.

## Generated artifacts retain source paths

Three generated Qt build links under
`package/desktop-app/file-manager-qt/target/debug/build/**/out/cxxqtbuild/include/`
were absolute links into `/var/home/user/Monochromatic`.
From the copied tree they resolved outside the destination and back into the source checkout.

One package-manager link was already dangling in both source and destination:

```text
package/claude-code-plugin/source/node_modules/@monochromatic-dev/claude-code-plugins-hook-types
  -> ../../../hook-types
```

A relocation audit must resolve complete link chains and detect:

- absolute links outside the destination;
- relative links whose resolved target escapes the destination;
- dangling links;
- loops;
- links introduced through selected ignored state.

Derived state such as `node_modules`, `target`, build output, incremental caches, reports, and temporary files
must be regenerated or omitted by default rather than treated as portable checkout state.
Binary and native artifacts also need checks for embedded source paths, debug paths, and runtime search paths.

## Tracked operational files contain machine paths

Current path-sensitive tracked files include:

- `.idea/gradle.xml:16`, which stores an absolute Gradle module path;
- `.idea/vcs.xml:9`, which duplicates the project-relative mapping with an absolute VCS mapping;
- `package/desktop-daemon/hall-monitor/hall-monitor.desktop:5`, whose `Exec` launches the source checkout's binary;
- `package/desktop-daemon/hall-monitor/src/analyze/llama.ts:15`, `:20`, and `:25`, which hardcode a model,
  projector, and `llama-server` under one user's home;
- `package/figma/kiwi/src/verify.ts:20`, which hardcodes one user's Figma export directory.

Historical documentation and adversarial path fixtures may intentionally contain absolute paths.
A portability audit must distinguish those from operational source, launchers, IDE configuration, and generated output.
Any exception needs a narrow allowlist entry with a rationale.

## User-global integrations remain bound to the source

Current user configuration contains active source-checkout bindings:

- `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` points nine Pi extensions at `/var/home/user/Monochromatic/package/pi-plugin/*`.
- `~/.claude/settings.json:48` launches the statusline from `/var/home/user/Monochromatic`.

A raw copy cannot decide which of two coexisting checkouts should own these global integrations.
Silently retargeting them during a copy would be unsafe.
Activation must be an explicit,
transactional operation with a preview, backup, rollback, and ownership report.
Project-scoped integration should be preferred wherever the host supports it.

The tracked Hall Monitor desktop entry has the same ownership problem when installed into user desktop or systemd state.
The repository needs install-time generation or a stable installed artifact,
not a tracked launcher tied to one checkout.

## Trust, secrets, tools, and external resources are intentional host seams

A copied path was untrusted according to `mise trust --show`.
Destination trust must remain an explicit user decision and must never be copied from the source.
Both the root configuration and `mise.local.toml`, when present, need to parse without hidden trust assumptions.

`.env.local.json` is encrypted and gitignored.
Mise decrypts it using the external identity at `~/.config/mise/age.txt` as documented in `mise.toml:1159-1165`.
The identity must not be bundled into a checkout.
Copying the encrypted file should require an explicit local-state profile.

A functional host also supplies Mise itself, managed tools, system packages, Podman images, Android SDK state,
GUI and systemd facilities, Hall Monitor models and `llama-server`, and Kiwi's external data.
The repository currently targets Fedora Linux according to `README.md:244-249`.
These are host-contract dependencies, not checkout contents.
A fresh machine remains a bootstrap scenario through `README.md:97-139`, not a zero-setup file copy.

# Why arbitrary raw copy cannot be the supported interface

Raw copy cannot guarantee relocation correctness for arbitrary repository state:

- `cp` does not acquire a coherent Git or worktree snapshot.
- Copying a live tree can mix files from different moments.
- `cp --recursive`, `cp --archive`, dereferencing modes, and cross-filesystem behavior differ.
- Copying `.git` imports worktree registrations, reflogs, hooks, local config, credentials, and stale metadata.
- Copying nested worktrees preserves absolute links to their original common Git directory.
- Copying ignored build state preserves path-bearing generated artifacts.
- External user settings cannot infer which coexisting copy should become active.
- User trust and decryption keys should not become portable by copying them.

A frozen tree that already contains no path dependencies can be copied successfully.
This repository's measured state does not meet that condition.

# Proposed design

Create a deep checkout-relocation module with a small repository interface:

```sh
# Create an independent destination from the current checkout.
mise run checkout:copy -- DEST

# Add only a declared, portable ignored-state profile.
mise run checkout:copy -- DEST --state=developer

# Audit the current checkout, or an explicit path, without mutation.
mise run checkout:audit
mise run checkout:audit -- PATH

# Preview or explicitly activate integrations for the current checkout.
mise run checkout:activate -- --pi --claude --desktop --dry-run
mise run checkout:activate -- --pi --claude --desktop

# Restore the previous integration ownership captured by activation.
mise run checkout:activate -- --undo
```

The interface should hide snapshotting, Git reconstruction, state classification,
path auditing, integration adapters, reporting, and rollback.

## `checkout:copy`

`checkout:copy` should:

1. Require an absent or empty destination outside the source tree.
2. Refuse an unborn HEAD, sparse checkout, submodules, or an in-progress merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert,
   or bisect until each state has an explicit preservation contract.
3. Support invocation from either a main worktree or a linked worktree.
4. Create a coherent selected-state snapshot.
   Build an immutable manifest of selected Git and filesystem state,
   copy into a private stage,
   then require the source manifest and Git identity to remain identical before publication.
   Source mutation must fail rather than publish a mixed destination.
5. Construct a new independent Git repository instead of copying source `.git` and repairing it.
6. Preserve reachable local commits and refs, current HEAD, staged changes, unstaged tracked changes,
   and non-ignored untracked files.
7. Avoid object alternates, shared object databases, mutable hard-linked Git files, copied reflogs,
   copied hooks, copied worktree registrations, copied local credentials, and copied commit-graph state.
8. Exclude ignored state by default.
9. Allow only named, tracked profiles of portable ignored state.
   The initial `developer` profile may include `mise.local.toml` and other reviewed machine-neutral local config,
   but must exclude `.env.local.json`, `node_modules`, `target`, caches, reports, temp files,
   nested worktrees, and Git administration unless each entry is explicitly opted in.
10. Regenerate package-manager links and other required derived state through existing Mise tasks.
11. Run `checkout:audit` before atomically publishing the destination.
12. Leave the source unchanged after both success and failure.
13. Remove private staging after success and safely retain diagnosable state after an ownership-ambiguous failure.
14. Emit redacted human-readable and JSON reports describing preserved state, omitted state,
    required bootstrap work, external host dependencies, and integration activation status.

## `checkout:audit`

`checkout:audit` should report and fail on:

- Git administration that refers to another common directory;
- copied linked-worktree registrations not owned by the destination;
- Git alternates or shared mutable object state;
- credential material in repository-local Git URLs or config;
- operational text or binary content containing the canonical source checkout path;
- resolved-outside-root, dangling, or cyclic links outside a narrow reviewed allowlist;
- tracked operational absolute user paths;
- generated launchers tied to another checkout;
- undeclared external host resources.

The audit should report intentional external seams separately:

- untrusted destination Mise configuration;
- absent encrypted local secrets or age identity;
- missing host tools and system facilities;
- missing models, servers, or datasets;
- inactive Pi, Claude, desktop, and systemd integrations.

## `checkout:activate`

Activation should:

- derive the checkout root from the task's current repository;
- display current owner, requested owner, and exact files or registrations to change;
- require explicit selection and confirmation;
- offer `--dry-run`;
- back up modified user configuration with restrictive permissions;
- apply changes transactionally;
- be idempotent;
- support `--undo`;
- never modify an unrelated checkout;
- prefer project-scoped registration over global registration;
- redact credentials and unrelated settings from output.

Adapters are justified here because Pi, Claude, desktop launchers,
and systemd each provide distinct real integration mechanisms.

# Required path remediations

- Replace `.idea` absolute module and VCS paths with `$PROJECT_DIR$`-relative configuration.
- Generate Hall Monitor's desktop entry at install time or install the built binary to a stable user location.
- Make Hall Monitor model, projector, and server locations explicit configuration with validated errors.
- Make Kiwi's source directory an argument or explicit configuration rather than a user path in source.
- Replace documentation that instructs users to paste checkout-specific Pi paths with the activation task.
- Move the Git LFS credential to a credential helper or secret injection and rotate the exposed value.
- Exclude or rebuild Qt, Rust, pnpm, Electron, and other path-bearing derived output.
- Add a tracked operational-path portability policy with reviewed fixture and documentation exclusions.

# Options considered

## Canonical independent copy command

Pros:

- Creates coherent Git and worktree state rather than repairing copied administration.
- Centralizes portability, security, state selection, reporting, and verification behind one interface.
- Can fail transactionally before publishing an unsafe destination.

Cons:

- Adds a repository-specific command and implementation.
- Users must choose it instead of arbitrary raw copy.
- Preserving index and worktree state needs careful Git plumbing and fixture coverage.

## Post-copy repair command

Pros:

- Fits an existing `cp` workflow.
- Could diagnose and remove common stale generated state.

Cons:

- Cannot prove the source copy was coherent.
- Starts from copied credentials, hooks, reflogs, and worktree administration.
- Cannot reliably distinguish intended local state from copied garbage after the source context is lost.
- Has a larger destructive repair surface.

## Make arbitrary raw copy transparent

Pros:

- Requires no new copy command.
- Matches the simplest user expectation.

Cons:

- Would require banning or externalizing linked worktrees, nested worktrees, path-bearing generated output,
  repository-local credentials, and checkout-specific integrations.
- Still cannot choose global integration ownership when two copies coexist.
- Still should not copy trust state or decryption identities.
- Cannot guarantee a coherent snapshot of a live tree.

Ranking: canonical independent copy command > post-copy repair command > arbitrary raw-copy transparency.
The canonical command ranks above repair because it controls snapshot and Git construction before publication.
Repair ranks above raw transparency because it can at least diagnose copied state,
while raw transparency cannot resolve dynamic Git state or global ownership safely.

# Acceptance criteria

## Independent destination

- The destination remains functional after the source path is renamed, unmounted, or made inaccessible in a fixture.
- `git worktree list` contains only destination-owned registrations.
- No nested `.git` file resolves to the source common Git directory.
- No destination Git object alternate, shared object database,
  or mutable hard-linked Git administration depends on source.
- No repository-local Git URL or config contains credential material.
- `git status`, branch creation, a fixture commit, fetch, and an LFS operation succeed without touching source.
- `git fsck` and `git lfs fsck` pass in the independent destination.

## Preserved state

- Local commits and refs are preserved.
- Current HEAD and branch or detached state are preserved.
- Staged content remains staged.
- Unstaged tracked content remains unstaged.
- Non-ignored untracked files are preserved.
- Ignored state is absent unless selected by a named profile.
- Unsupported Git states fail before destination publication with actionable diagnostics.

## Path independence

- No operational file, Git administrative record, generated launcher, binary runtime path,
  or resolved link references the source checkout.
- Historical documentation and adversarial fixtures are allowed only through narrow reviewed exclusions.
- External host resources appear in a redacted dependency report rather than as hidden hardcoded paths.
- Hall Monitor, Kiwi, IDE configuration, and Pi, Claude, desktop,
  and systemd integration findings are each remediated or declared as explicit host seams.

## Transaction and security behavior

- Source files, source Git state, and source user integrations remain unchanged after copy success and failure.
- Failure publishes no partially usable destination.
- Activation preview, apply, idempotent repeat, failure rollback, and `--undo` are tested.
- No secret, credential-bearing Git config, trust state, decryption identity,
  model, or external dataset is copied by default.
- Every report and diagnostic redacts credentials and unrelated user settings.

## Verification coverage

Disposable fixtures cover:

- a main worktree and linked source worktree;
- multiple linked-worktree registrations;
- a nested `.git` file;
- staged, unstaged, untracked, and ignored state;
- local commits and detached HEAD;
- absolute, escaping-relative, chained, dangling, and cyclic links;
- path-bearing generated and binary artifacts;
- a credential-bearing local Git URL;
- a source mutation race;
- an unsupported in-progress Git operation;
- destination collision and destination-inside-source rejection;
- activation dry-run, apply, rollback, and undo for each adapter.

End-user verification must exercise the destination through Mise,
Git and Git LFS,
a representative TypeScript build and test,
a representative Rust or native rebuild,
and the host applications for every integration adapter.

# Immediate security action

Revoke or rotate the credential currently embedded in local `.git/config` before portability implementation begins.
Do not paste its value into this issue, commits, logs, test fixtures, or command transcripts.
Move future authentication to a credential helper or secret-injection mechanism,
then verify that `checkout:audit` detects a credential-bearing URL without printing it.

## Symptom

While resolving #270, package-scoped verification for `@monochromatic-dev/ssg-aquati.cat` could not complete through `buildAndTest` because the i18n generation step crashed before the targeted unit test ran.

Command:

```sh
mise run buildAndTest -- packages/ssg/aquati.cat/src/components/question-id.unit.test.ts
```

Failing task:

```txt
[//packages/ssg/aquati.cat:build:i18n] $ typesafe-i18n --no-watch
```

Error:

```txt
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: No "exports" main defined in /var/home/user/Monochromatic/node_modules/.pnpm/typesafe-i18n@5.27.1_typescript@7.0.1-rc/node_modules/typescript/package.json imported from /var/home/user/Monochromatic/node_modules/.pnpm/typesafe-i18n@5.27.1_typescript@7.0.1-rc/node_modules/typesafe-i18n/cli/typesafe-i18n.mjs
    at exportsNotFound (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:315:10)
    at packageExportsResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:663:9)
    at packageResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:792:12)
    at moduleResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:873:18)
    at defaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:1006:11)
```

Observed runtime:

```txt
Node.js v26.4.0
```

## Current evidence

- `packages/ssg/aquati.cat/mise.toml` runs i18n generation as `typesafe-i18n --no-watch`.
- `packages/ssg/aquati.cat/package.json` has `typesafe-i18n` and `typescript` in `devDependencies` using the default catalog.
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves that pair as `typesafe-i18n@5.27.1(typescript@7.0.1-rc)`.
- The workspace also carries a `classic` TypeScript catalog entry for packages that need the classic compiler API.
- The targeted unit test itself passed when run directly through `mise run test -- packages/ssg/aquati.cat/src/components/question-id.unit.test.ts`, so this issue is about the package build precondition, not the quiz hash test.

## Suspected cause

`typesafe-i18n` imports the `typescript` package from its CLI. In this workspace, that peer resolves to the native TypeScript 7 RC package, whose package export surface does not provide a main entry that Node can import as `typescript` from `typesafe-i18n/cli/typesafe-i18n.mjs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `mise run //packages/ssg/aquati.cat:build:i18n` succeeds.
- `mise run buildAndTest -- packages/ssg/aquati.cat/src/components/question-id.unit.test.ts` reaches the package build and test successfully.
- The selected fix is documented in package metadata or troubleshooting docs if it depends on pinning `typesafe-i18n` to classic TypeScript.

## Candidate fixes to evaluate

- Move `packages/ssg/aquati.cat`'s `typescript` devDependency to `catalog:classic` if `typesafe-i18n` needs classic TypeScript.
- Split i18n generation into a wrapper task that supplies a compatible TypeScript package only to `typesafe-i18n`.
- Upgrade or patch `typesafe-i18n` if upstream has added TypeScript 7 RC compatibility.

## Session baseline

The ergonomic implementation session landed:

- `3ef6fed29`,
  complete writable-path diagnostics,
  source ownership guidance,
  local producer attribution,
  cache omissions,
  and foreign observer provenance;
- `b2078262d`,
  explicit callback `this` alignment,
  deterministic ordering,
  mixed declaration ownership,
  bound return-flow attribution,
  and schema-7 reason persistence;
- `f850dd98f`,
  schema-8 specific omission reasons and lint-level cold,
  warm,
  fixed-worker,
  and default-worker fingerprint parity.

Issue #430 closed through the implementation commit.
The three extracted effect rules remain disabled as requested.

## Work intentionally not completed

### Observer-return retention remains conflated with opacity

Issue #427 records that an identity observer such as `rows.map(row => row)` can withhold a readonly preference correctly
while also becoming an unexplained opaque effect.
This session did not add a retention-specific relation,
collection call identity,
or persistent provenance for that distinction.

Required follow-up:

- preserve preference withholding when observer output retains receiver state;
- keep retention out of `no-opaque-parameter-effects` unless callback performs a genuinely unresolved operation;
- preserve exact member and call-site provenance through clone,
  serialization,
  validation,
  and cache restoration;
- cover identity `map`,
  wrapped `map`,
  `map` plus `toSorted`,
  `flatMap`,
  nested owned callers,
  and a warm persistent-cache process.

### Extracted-rule rollout remains gated

Issue #423 still owns workspace rollout for:

- `no-readonly-parameter-mutations`;
- `no-opaque-parameter-effects`;
- `no-invalid-parameter-effect-contracts`.

This session did not establish the post-retention whole-workspace finding fingerprint,
remediate or accept every stable site,
extend the self-hosting override,
or change shared severities from `off` to `error`.
The disposable omission fixture proves cache and worker parity at the Oxlint boundary,
but it is not the #423 workspace acceptance sweep.

### Remaining named-boundary guidance was not reclassified

Issue #427 still records heterogeneous valid opacity findings.
This session did not:

- give `flat` collection-specific guidance;
- add a reviewed acceptance manifest for dynamic callable boundaries;
- weaken `JSON.stringify` opacity for unproved object graphs;
- add package,
  type,
  or member allow-lists.

The final three choices are intentional non-changes.
Getters,
`toJSON`,
replacers,
and proxies remain executable channels,
and declaration identity remains insufficient runtime ownership evidence.

### Semantic filesystem snapshots remain separate

Issue #441 still owns run-frozen semantic filesystem design.
This session did not change retained overlay deletion behavior or replace live delegated filesystem reads with one
run-consistent view.

### Narrow instruction placement remains undecided

- Issue #451 decides where living-handover maintenance pointers belong.
- Issue #452 decides where the no-character-budget and no-path-count-budget behavior contract belongs.

Root `AGENTS.md` was intentionally unchanged.
No scheduler was introduced.

## Recommended order

1. Separate observer-return retention from unresolved opacity under #427.
2. Take the stable full-workspace fingerprint and complete #423 remediation or reviewed acceptance.
3. Enable the three extracted rules directly at `error` only after #423 acceptance passes.
4. Handle #441 as a separate semantic snapshot architecture track.
5. Resolve #451 and #452 by choosing package-local discovery locations.

## Completion criteria

This remainder issue can close when:

- every item is completed in its canonical linked issue,
  explicitly rejected there,
  or superseded by a documented decision;
- #427 no longer lists an unimplemented ergonomic defect from this session;
- #423 records a stable workspace fingerprint and final severity decision;
- #441 records its snapshot decision independently;
- #451 and #452 have placement decisions;
- `doc/handover/prefer-readonly-parameter-types-issue-review.md` reflects every disposition.

## Goal

Promote these shared Oxlint rules directly from `off` to `error`:

- `prefer-readonly-parameter-type/no-readonly-parameter-mutations`;
- `prefer-readonly-parameter-type/no-opaque-parameter-effects`;
- `prefer-readonly-parameter-type/no-invalid-parameter-effect-contracts`.

Do not introduce a warning phase.
`prefer-readonly-parameter-type/prefer-readonly-parameter-types` is already enforced at `error` and is not part of this promotion.

## Why they start disabled

Issue #422 split one multi-purpose diagnostic into operation-specific policies.
The shared workspace is ready for proved readonly replacements,
but it has not yet remediated or reviewed every proved readonly mutation,
unresolved effect,
and invalid effect-contract finding.

Keeping the extracted rules present but disabled makes the intended final policy explicit without breaking unrelated workspace work during the migration.

## Readiness paths

Every finding must reach one of these reviewed states:

- code or type changes remove the behavior;
- verified intrinsic,
  source,
  source-map,
  or effect modeling proves the behavior;
- an accurate effect contract records every known effect;
- a site-specific acceptance manifest records irreducible uncertainty.

A reviewed acceptance manifest must use stable site fingerprints,
reject changed sites,
and report stale entries for removal.
Package-wide overrides and inline disable comments are not acceptance mechanisms.

## Completion criteria

- [ ] Inventory each disabled rule across the full workspace.
- [ ] Resolve or explicitly accept every finding through one readiness path.
- [ ] Implement and test the acceptance manifest if any finding needs it.
- [ ] Decide whether extracted rules need no-disable guards after the acceptance mechanism is known.
- [ ] Extend the plugin package's self-hosting override to all three extracted rules before enabling them.
- [ ] Verify all three rules at `error` through the shared Oxlint configuration.
- [ ] Remove the temporary configuration comments and change all three entries directly from `off` to `error` in one commit.
- [ ] Run affected package lint tasks and a full workspace lint with zero errors or warnings attributable to these rules.

## Evidence

The design,
prototype,
and split-rule implementation are recorded in:

- #422;
- `doc/planning/prefer-readonly-positive-evidence.md`;
- `doc/handover/prefer-readonly-diagnostic-split.md`.
